 Oral Judgment
1.
The claimant is in appeal challenging the dismissal of his claim petition.

2. The claimant approached the Tribunal with a claim petition contending that while he was riding pillion on the motor-cycle owned by his father, which was being driven by his relative Yogesh on 09.06.2016, the motor-cycle met with an accident when Yogesh rode over the road-bump in a rash and negligent manner, as a result of which, both of them fell down and the claimant suffered injuries to his face.

3. The Tribunal has refused to accept his plea and has dismissed the claim petition on the ground that the NC: 2024:KHC:51088 accident occurred on 09.06.2016 but the First Information Report ('FIR') was lodged only on 15.06.2016 i.e., after about six days.
4.
The Tribunal has also noticed that there were discrepancies in the medical records regarding the time of the accident and, therefore, there was reason to suspect foul play.

The Tribunal has also observed that it was the case of the claimant that the rider of the motor-cycle i.e., Yogesh had also suffered some injuries and since no documents to that effect were produced, there was reason to suspect foul play regarding the person who was driving the motorcycle.
5.
In my view, this reasoning of the Tribunal cannot be accepted.

The medical records which are produced including the Medico-Legal Case Register Exhibit P- 12(a) indicates that the claimant was brought to the hospital with an alleged history of a road traffic NC: 2024:KHC:51088 accident which occurred on 09.06.2016 at around 3.30 p.m.
6.

If the victim of a motor vehicle accident approaches a hospital, complains of injuries being suffered and informs the hospital that he had suffered injuries as a result of a motor vehicle accident, primarily, the obligation is on the hospital to inform the police authorities.

If the H K Jeevan vs H T Krishna Kumar on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22853104/
2 information is given or even if the information is not given by the hospital authorities, the said act cannot prejudice the claimant in making a claim for compensation.

sentences.text: 7. It is to be stated here that in law, the victim of a motor vehicle accident is not obliged to register an FIR and it is also to be noticed that at the time of the accident, the primary interest of the victim and his relatives would be to ensure that he approaches an hospital so as to get the best possible medical care.
In this view of the matter, the reasoning of the Tribunal that there was a delay of six days in lodging an FIR would be incorrect.

9. As far as the discrepancies in the medical records regarding the manner of the accident, it is to be stated here that even in the medical Medico-Legal Case Register, there is a clear statement that the claimant was in a semi-conscious state.
10. In the case-sheet, it is also stated that the patient was semi-conscious and was mildly disoriented.
If the claimant was semi-conscious and disoriented, the entries made in the case-sheet as to the manner in which the accident occurred would not really be of any significance.

11. As already stated, the moment a victim approaches the hospital and informs them about an accident, the obligation, if any, of the claimant in informing the authorities stands eclipsed and I am,
therefore, of NC: 2024:KHC:51088 the view that the Tribunal was not justified in dismissing the claim petition and hence, the findings in this regard are accordingly set aside.

12. Though under the normal circumstances the matter would have been remanded to the Tribunal for consideration of the compensation payable, having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year 2016, it would be unfair to relegate the parties to the Tribunal.
Consequently, the assessment of compensation is also undertaken in this appeal.
13. The doctor who treated the claimant was examined as PW-2.
He has opined that the claimant had suffered an 8% disability in respect of his facial fractures.
The doctor has also stated that the claimant has facial disfigurement and is not able to chew hard-food and he has pareshesia of right side of the lower lip.
In my view, in light of this evidence, it would be appropriate to treat the whole body disability of the claimant at 10%.

15. As the claimant was aged about 19 years as on the date of the accident and was studying Engineering, it would be appropriate to adopt the notional income of Rs.9,500/- determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accidents of the year 2016.

would have to be applied.
17. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,05,200/- (Rs.9,500/- x 12 x '18' x 10%) towards 'loss of future income'.
